statement: You are given a directed graph: the vertex count V (vertices 0 to V − 1) and a list of edges [u, v], each pointing from u to v. The graph may have several parts that are not connected to each other.
A directed cycle is a path that follows edges in their direction and comes back to the vertex it started from.
Return true if the graph contains at least one directed cycle, and false otherwise.
This version uses depth-first search and remembers which vertices are on the current recursion path: an edge into a vertex that is still on the path closes a cycle.

examples.explanation: 0 → 1 → 2 → 0 follows the edges back to where it started.
Vertex 3 is reached along two routes, but every edge points forward, so no path returns to its start.
The part 0 → 1 has no cycle, but in the separate part 2 and 3 point at each other.
